name: Namibia
gaps: Namibia has no BirdLife International partner organization. The Namibia Crane Working Group is supported by the Namibia Nature Foundation but details are unavailable for independent verification.

groups.name: Namibia Bird Club
groups.blurb: Ornithological society founded in 1962, running guided walks and surveys. Publishes journal Lanioturdus and newsletter Bird Call.

name: Botswana
gaps: No regional bird club structure with separate websites. BirdLife Botswana coordinates with community groups but specific local clubs are not listed on their public site.

groups.name: BirdLife Botswana
groups.blurb: The national BirdLife partner, formerly the Botswana Bird Club. Runs education, research and community mobilization for bird conservation.

name: Zimbabwe
gaps: BirdLife Zimbabwe works with Site Support Groups and local branches but specific regional branch details are not listed on their public site. A Birdlife Youth Club Zimbabwe and Everyday Birds Zimbabwe Facebook group are mentioned regionally but could not be independently verified.

groups.name: BirdLife Zimbabwe
groups.blurb: The national bird society and BirdLife partner, founded 1951. Coordinates branches and citizen science atlassing and bird record submission.

name: Zambia
gaps: BirdWatch Zambia is the only birding organization with significant public presence. Other groups (African Cuckoos, Zambia Barn Swallow Project) focus on research rather than community birding activities.

groups.name: BirdWatch Zambia
groups.blurb: The national BirdLife partner founded 1969. Runs monthly bird walks, citizen science and monitoring of 42 Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas.

name: Malawi
gaps: Regional branches (Balaka, Blantyre, Dwangwa, Lilongwe, Monkeybay, Mulanje, Mzuza, Nkhatabay, Zomba) have limited individual web presence and operate through the main WESM site and affiliated wildlife clubs.

groups.name: Wildlife and Environmental Society of Malawi
groups.blurb: The national BirdLife partner, founded 1947. Operates through nine regional branches and over 1500 community wildlife clubs.

name: Mozambique
gaps: No BirdLife International partner. Birds Mozambique and AACEM mentioned in regional resources but no independently verified online presence. No findable community for local birders.

name: Madagascar
gaps: Asity Madagascar's direct website unavailable. Madagascar Birding Association mentioned regionally but could not be independently verified with published content.

groups.name: Asity Madagascar
groups.blurb: The national BirdLife partner and 100 percent Malagasy organization protecting endemic birds through environmental education and community conservation.

groups.name: The Peregrine Fund Madagascar
groups.blurb: Community conservation program that rediscovered four presumed extinct bird species and has fostered over 30 community associations around protected areas.

name: Mauritius
gaps: Council for Nature Conservation mentioned regionally but not independently verified. No bird atlas or structured citizen science scheme found.

groups.name: Mauritian Wildlife Foundation
groups.blurb: The national BirdLife partner and largest conservation NGO in Mauritius. Renowned for saving endemic birds from extinction through research and conservation.

name: Seychelles
gaps: Seychelles Bird Records Committee exists but independent website not found. Island Conservation Society mentioned regionally but current status unverified.

groups.name: Nature Seychelles
groups.blurb: The national BirdLife partner managing conservation of endemic species. Manages Cousin Island Special Reserve and runs island restoration and seabird protection.

groups.name: Seychelles Islands Foundation
groups.blurb: Manages UNESCO World Heritage sites Aldabra Atoll and Vallée de Mai, protecting endemic and seabird populations including the Seychelles black parrot.

groups.name: SEOR
groups.blurb: Ornithological society founded 1997, studying and conserving Reunion's endemic birds. Operates wildlife rescue center with 20 staff and 250 active members.

name: Comoros
gaps: No BirdLife International partner. Conservation organizations (Dahari, Blue Ventures) focus on marine and habitat conservation rather than community birding. No findable birding community.

name: Lesotho
gaps: No BirdLife International partner. BirdLife Lesotho mentioned on regional pages but current activity and independent web presence could not be verified.

name: Eswatini
gaps: No BirdLife International partner. The Natural History Society of Eswatini mentioned regionally but no confirmed public website or verified current activity.

groups.name: Birds Angola
groups.blurb: Ornithological organization supporting research and conservation of Angolan birds. Provides expertise to birders, researchers and conservation professionals.
